content.value_statement: Layout-heavy animations and overlapping tweens can cause visible jank. This skill guides your assistant toward transform-based motion, batched updates, reusable tweens, and targeted cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Recommend transform and opacity animations instead of layout-heavy properties when the visual result permits.
Explain selective will-change usage and batching DOM reads before writes.
Suggest stagger, visible-item animation, and timeline reuse for large element collections.
Show gsap.quickTo usage for frequently updated properties such as pointer-following motion.
Guide ScrollTrigger pinning, scrub testing, and refresh timing after layout changes.
Recommend pausing or killing inactive animations and reducing simultaneous animation work.
limitations: Provides written guidance and examples, not an executable profiler or automated benchmark suite.
Cannot guarantee 60fps; results depend on page complexity, browser behavior, and target devices.
Requires a project with GSAP available to apply its JavaScript examples.
References separate skills for core animation, timelines, and deeper ScrollTrigger coverage.

use_cases.title: Reduce Interface Animation Jank
use_cases.description: Review component animations for layout-heavy properties, repeated DOM layout, and unnecessary concurrent tweens.

use_cases.title: Improve Pointer-Following Motion
use_cases.description: Replace repeated tween creation during pointer movement with reusable quickTo updates.

use_cases.title: Review Scroll Animation Workload
use_cases.description: Assess pinning, refresh frequency, inactive animation cleanup, and low-end device testing before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Single Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GSAP animation: [animation code]. Identify layout-heavy properties and suggest transform or opacity alternatives that preserve the intended appearance.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Pointer Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pointer-following animation: [animation code]. Use gsap.quickTo where appropriate and explain how it avoids creating a new tween on every update.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate optimization of frequently updated properties.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce List Animation Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this animated list: [component code]. Suggest stagger, timeline reuse, visible-item animation, and batched DOM reads and writes where applicable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of many animated elements.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Scroll Animation Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this GSAP page: [page code]. Prioritize pinning, scrub settings, refresh calls, concurrent tweens, and cleanup, then propose low-end device checks without claiming unmeasured gains.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review across a scroll-driven page.

output_examples.input: A panel moves by animating left and top, and the transition feels uneven.
output: Use transform-based x and y movement if it preserves the intended layout.
Collect required DOM measurements before applying animation updates.
Test the transition on target devices before concluding that rendering improved.

output_examples.input: A pointer follower creates new tweens on every mousemove event.
output: Create reusable quickTo handlers for the horizontal and vertical properties.
Pass updated pointer coordinates to those handlers instead of creating separate tweens.
Review animation cleanup when the component becomes inactive.

output_examples.input: A long scrolling page refreshes ScrollTrigger frequently and keeps hidden animations running.
output: Refresh after actual layout changes and debounce repeated refresh requests where appropriate.
Pause or kill inactive animations and limit unnecessary pinning.
Check scroll behavior on low-end devices before accepting scrub setting changes.

best_practices: Prefer transform and opacity when they preserve the intended visual result.
Reuse timelines and quickTo handlers, and batch DOM reads before writes.
Test representative low-end devices and clean up animations when they become inactive.
anti_patterns: Animate width, height, top, or left for movement when transforms can produce the same result.
Apply will-change or force3D to every element without a specific animation need.
Create overlapping tweens or ScrollTriggers without testing performance and handling cleanup.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee smooth 60fps animation?
faq.answer: No. It provides optimization guidance; actual frame rates require testing on your page and target devices.

faq.question: Does it install GSAP or run benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. The supplied file contains guidance and examples, not installation scripts or benchmark tooling.

faq.question: When is gsap.quickTo useful?
faq.answer: Use it for frequently updated properties, such as pointer-following x and y values, to reuse a tween instead of repeatedly creating tweens.

faq.question: Does it cover ScrollTrigger performance?
faq.answer: It covers selective pinning, scrub testing, refresh timing, and cleanup. It references a separate skill for broader ScrollTrigger guidance.

faq.question: Should will-change be applied to every element?
faq.answer: No. The guidance recommends using it selectively on elements that animate, rather than applying it everywhere.
